 Why Florida is still seeing storms after the rainy season 
 By Ric Kearbey Published : Nov. 20, 2026 at 5:14 PM EST | Updated : 4 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SARASOTA, Fla. ( WWSB ) - Showers and thunderstorms remain in the forecast in Florida, even though the state’s rainy season typically winds down in October, ABC 7 First Alert meteorologist Rick Kirby said.
 Kirby said the end of the rainy season does not mean the rain stops.
 During summer, afternoon thunderstorms are fueled by intense sunshine, abundant moisture and daily sea breezes, Kirby said.
 In November, cold fronts, upper-level disturbances and changing wind patterns become more important, he said. Kirby said that is what Florida is seeing this week.
 Florida’s normally dry season could get a boost this winter from a likely strong El Niño, Kirby said. El Niño refers to unusually warm waters near the equator in the Pacific Ocean.
 Kirby said the biggest impact for Florida is a more active southern jet stream, which typically sends additional storm systems across the state throughout the winter.
 He said El Niño could also increase the chance of strong to severe thunderstorms during the winter.
